ZOZO confirms ZOZOTOWN and WEAR customer.summary: ZOZO reported exposure of member data through PLAID’s KARTE marketing platform. It gave separate counts of about 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN members and 13.93 million WEAR members, with overlap unknown.
attack_chain: Unauthorized access occurred at the third-party marketing platform.
ZOZO learned of the intrusion and stopped data transfers to KARTE.
ZOZO confirmed some connected customer and business contact information had been exposed. Passwords and payment-card details were not affected.
open_questions: How many people appear in both affected groups?
What retained vendor data can be removed to limit future exposure?
mitigations: Share only fields required by vendor integrations and remove data associated with closed accounts where retention is not required.
Revoke unused integration access and review vendor audit records.
Warn affected customers about targeted phishing and publish notification instructions on official channels.

sources.label: Yahoo! News Japan reporting on ZOZO’s disclosure

Equinor cyberattack linked to Azure API.summary: Norway’s National Security Authority said attackers exploited Microsoft Azure API Management against Equinor and other organisations. The authority said the flaw was fixed; Equinor said it stopped the intrusion and reported no indication of stolen data or production impact.
attack_chain: The regulator attributed the intrusion to a vulnerability in a managed Azure service.
Equinor detected unauthorized activity on November 17 and mobilized its response teams.
Equinor announced containment on November 20; Norway’s regulator said the flaw had been fixed.
open_questions: Which customer environments were affected?
What evidence is available to customers to determine whether their own environments were reached?
mitigations: Review communications and exposure guidance from Microsoft and the national security authority.
Preserve Azure activity, identity and gateway logs and investigate anomalous management actions.
Review privileged roles and rotate any secrets shown by investigation to be exposed.

Peach Aviation discloses Cuenote vendor.summary: Peach Aviation reported 8,997,106 affected customer records after a breach at email vendor Yumirulink. The count does not establish unique individuals, and the airline said passport and payment-card information was not affected.
attack_chain: Initial intrusion method: not disclosed in Peach’s notice.
Unauthorized access occurred at the service provider on October 18; Peach later confirmed the scope of its affected records.
Peach said it would begin notifying affected customers on November 20.
open_questions: How did unauthorized access begin?
How many unique people do the records represent?
mitigations: Minimize customer data stored in email-delivery services and enforce retention limits.
Review vendor access and audit logs, and conduct joint incident response exercises.
Direct customers to verified company channels and warn about breach-themed impersonation.

Microsoft Agent Framework PyPI supply-ch.summary: Researchers identified unauthorized Microsoft Agent Framework releases on PyPI that targeted cloud and CI credentials. The releases were quarantined, but affected organizations still need to assess whether credentials were exposed.
attack_chain: Unauthorized package releases appeared on PyPI on November 17; how the publisher was compromised was not established.
The releases could expose credentials when run in affected environments.
PyPI quarantined the releases.
open_questions: Which downstream systems ran the affected releases?
What credentials were reachable and which were used?
mitigations: Remove affected releases, rebuild from reviewed dependencies, and purge affected caches.
Rotate credentials accessible to affected workloads and check their audit trails.
Use short-lived CI credentials and verify package provenance before installation.

Binance CEX.summary: Binance reported roughly $6.3 billion stolen in the October 29 incident. It obtained court orders to help recover assets, and blockchain monitors reported additional movements of funds attributed to the theft; these are developments in the original case, not a new loss.
attack_chain: Binance’s preliminary findings describe social engineering and compromise of employee devices.
Binance said the attacker misused an internal tool and gained unauthorized access to wallet signing operations.
Binance reported unauthorized transfers, then said it rebuilt the affected wallet environment, replaced devices and retired compromised credentials.
open_questions: How much has been returned, rather than frozen or tracked?
Which residual controls and assets remain subject to the investigation?
mitigations: Isolate wallet signing from employee devices and general-purpose internal tools.
Require independently verified approvals for large transfers and monitor changes to privileged access.
Keep recovery communications and coordination procedures ready with custodians and issuers.

sources.label: The National reporting on the theft and court orders

European Commission Confirms AI-Assisted.summary: The European Commission said an AI-assisted cyberattack detected in October led it to take several internal applications offline as a precaution. Most had been restored, and the Commission reported finding no evidence of a breach affecting staff as a whole while its investigation continued.
attack_chain: Initial access: not disclosed.
The Commission confirmed an AI-assisted campaign but has not publicly established its full scope.
The Commission took several applications offline as a precaution and restored most of them.
open_questions: Which systems, if any, experienced unauthorized access?
How did the campaign start and what remains offline?
Did it affect data or people outside the group covered by the Commission’s statement?
mitigations: Separate access to HR and reimbursement applications and require phishing-resistant authentication for privileged accounts.
Preserve application and identity logs and review for unusual access or bulk reads.
Test restoration from known-good backups and rehearse alternate workflows for essential internal services.

K3 Capital.summary: K3 Capital said roughly 3.43 million BOLD drained from its sBOLD vault on November 18 and traced the loss to the vault’s handling of collateral swaps. The project paused the vault and began pursuing partial recovery; it said Liquity V2 was not affected.
attack_chain: K3 identified a flaw in how the vault verified swaps and cleared token permissions.
The flawed workflow was abused to draw assets from the vault.
K3 paused the vault after nearly all its assets had been drained.
open_questions: How much will be returned to depositors?
What controls will be audited before the vault is used again?
mitigations: Verify swap results against observed asset balances and clear unused approvals.
Test with adversarial token and router behavior; add invariant tests for assets and shares.
Set abnormal outflow alerts and rehearse pausing affected vault operations.

Alleged hosting intrusion and Trubank ex.summary: VECERT Analyzer relayed a claim that a multi-tenant hosting environment and a system attributed to Trubank were accessed. The claim that 1,331 databases were affected is unverified; neither the hosting provider nor the number of people affected is established.
attack_chain: Initial access: unverified.
An outside party claimed unauthorized access to hosted databases and a system attributed to Trubank.
No extraction or exposure has been independently established.
open_questions: Can the host or affected tenants verify any unauthorized access?
Do the alleged records originate from the systems named in the claim?
mitigations: Preserve relevant hosting and database logs for investigation.
Audit public exposure of sensitive configuration and rotate any credentials found to be exposed.
Check tenant isolation and alert on unusual cross-tenant access or bulk exports.

Coinbase India INR withdrawal outage.summary: Coinbase India attributed unavailable in-app rupee withdrawals to an outage at its banking partner and said payouts were being processed in batches. Coinbase said its customers’ funds remained safe; the service disruption does not establish a breach or theft.
attack_chain: No attack has been substantiated.
Coinbase attributed the loss of in-app withdrawals to a partner payout outage.
Coinbase moved withdrawals to batch processing and routed new requests through support.
open_questions: When will in-app withdrawals return?
What caused the partner payout outage and how many users experienced delays?
mitigations: Monitor payout-provider health and reconcile retries against bank confirmations.
Test failover and duplicate-payment protection before rerouting payouts.
Publish status and support guidance through verified channels to reduce impersonation risk.

Vendor data breach exposes Chase, Visa,.summary: Chase said attackers accessed certain vendor-held marketing data, which may include customer names and email addresses. Mastercard confirmed limited email exposure in a cardholder benefit program, and Visa said a provider in Asia Pacific was affected but its own systems and payment data were not.
attack_chain: Initial access: not disclosed.
The companies reported incidents involving third-party service providers; whether the providers or intrusions overlap is unconfirmed.
Chase reported access to vendor-held marketing data, and Mastercard reported exposure of some cardholder email addresses.
open_questions: Which providers and systems were affected?
How many unique people were affected, and what data was exposed in each case?
mitigations: Limit how much personal information vendors retain and review their access regularly.
Ask vendors to preserve relevant logs and report bulk exports or unusual access promptly.
Warn affected customers about phishing and direct them to verified support channels.

Alleged EDUTEC Chile data exposure.summary: VECERT Analyzer relayed an unverified claim that more than 10 GB of records and photographs are linked to Chile's EDUTEC education platform. CiberLATAM tracked the same claim, but that coverage does not independently establish the data's origin, authenticity or scope.
attack_chain: Access and extraction: not established.
VECERT Analyzer reported a forum claim that the data had been obtained.
open_questions: Are the records authentic and attributable to EDUTEC?
Was there unauthorized access, and how many people, if any, were affected?
mitigations: Preserve access and export logs while investigating the claim.
Review who can access student records and photographs, and restrict bulk exports to authorized staff.
Prepare guidance for schools and families if exposure is verified.

Careers360.summary: Have I Been Pwned indexed a dataset attributed to the Indian education platform Careers360 that contains 3.6 million unique email addresses. The data also includes student entrance-exam results and other personal information; the initial access method has not been established.
attack_chain: Initial access and extraction: unknown.
A dataset attributed to Careers360 appeared on a public forum.
Have I Been Pwned indexed the affected email addresses.
open_questions: What system or third party was the source?
How many people, as opposed to unique email addresses, were affected?
mitigations: Restrict bulk access to student records with least privilege and approval gates.
Audit large exports and alert on unusual reads of student data.
Minimize retention of sensitive demographic data and limit access to exam results.

Too Lost.summary: Have I Been Pwned indexed data attributed to Too Lost containing about 724,000 unique email addresses. Some records contained password hashes, and a smaller subset contained identity verification or partial payment card details.
attack_chain: Initial access and extraction: unknown.
An unauthorized party claimed to have obtained Too Lost data.
Have I Been Pwned indexed the email addresses in the dataset.
open_questions: What systems were affected?
How many people had identity documents or financial details exposed?
mitigations: Isolate identity verification records and limit retention to required periods.
Require MFA for administrative access and monitor bulk downloads.
Revoke exposed credentials and active sessions if the investigation identifies compromised accounts.

Hackers steal data of 1.6 million SBC Me.summary: SBC Medical Group disclosed unauthorized access to website databases in Japan, affecting about 1.6 million people. A separate incident involved clinic administrator accounts at the Tribeau booking platform.
attack_chain: Initial access in both incidents: unknown.
In one incident, an intruder extracted records from the Japanese subsidiary's website databases.
In the separate Tribeau incident, unauthorized access to clinic administrator accounts exposed reservation or treatment-related information.
open_questions: How did each intrusion start?
Which data fields were exposed for each person?
mitigations: Segment public-facing services from customer records.
Require phishing-resistant MFA on clinic and third-party administrator accounts.
Monitor unusual database exports and retain access logs for investigation.

sources.label: BleepingComputer reporting on the SEC filing

Bell Canada says 'agentic' hacker stole.summary: Bell Canada said an intruder accessed some of its systems on November 17 and stole enterprise customer data. Bell said it contained the incident without disruption to customer services; the number of affected customers was not disclosed.
attack_chain: Initial access and the role of automation: not disclosed.
The intruder accessed systems including a pre-production circuit-provisioning environment.
Bell reported theft of some enterprise customer information and said it contained the intrusion.
open_questions: How was initial access gained?
How many customers were affected and which fields were taken?
mitigations: Keep real customer information out of pre-production where possible.
Segment provisioning systems and restrict service accounts to least privilege.
Log and alert on unusual access and bulk exports.

mitigations: Keep real customer information out of pre-production where possible.

Fluidkey.summary: Bitquery traced at least $1.58 million in unauthorized payouts across six chains. Fluidkey attributed the incident to exposed session data involving a third-party logging tool and restored service on an updated app. It says user keys remained on their devices; a full post-mortem is pending.
attack_chain: Fluidkey attributed exposure of session data to a third-party logging tool; it has not yet released a full technical account.
Bitquery traced unauthorized payouts through Fluidkey's relayer across six chains.
Fluidkey took services offline on November 19 and later restored access on v1.79.22 with older versions blocked.
open_questions: What is the complete timeline and scope of the logging-tool exposure?
What is the final loss after unclassified transactions are reconciled?
mitigations: Prevent session credentials from entering third-party logs and scope access to logging platforms.
Require explicit, independently verified confirmation for transactions.
Rate-limit and anomaly-check relayer submissions per account
Keep a tested kill switch for relayers

Wagyu (XMR1).summary: XMR1, Wagyu's bridged Monero token on Hyperliquid, fell from about $500 to $1 after roughly $13.5 million in sales. In a post-mortem, Wagyu's operator attributed the loss to a deployer key exposed in a breach at 1984.hosting; on-chain data corroborates the sales but not how the key was obtained.
attack_chain: Initial access (claimed): deployer key exposed through a breach at a hosting provider.
On-chain records show XMR1 transferred out of the deployer-controlled account; new minting was not established.
Roughly $13.5M of XMR1 is sold into Hyperliquid liquidity, collapsing the price from about $500 to $1.
On-chain analysis shows proceeds converted to ETH.
open_questions: Whether the compromise of the hosting provider exposed the key as the operator reported
What the final net losses are after any reimbursements
mitigations: Keep deployer and mint keys in HSM or multisig, never on hosting infrastructure
Remove or time-lock mint authority after deployment
Alert on mints and large sells from privileged addresses
